mainTopic: Idol worship as 'two evils,' why שמואל aged early, and the meal and parting of רב נחמן and רבי יצחק
overview: This amud begins by finishing an answer: the 'two evils' in ירמיהו are really one sin, עבודה זרה, which weighs as much as two. A ברייתא adds that the nations of כתים and קדר never left their false gods, yet the Jewish people left the true God. Next, רב נחמן asks how the פסוק can call שמואל 'old' when he died at fifty-two. רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן that old age jumped on him early. שמואל had prayed that שאול's kingship not be undone in his lifetime, so הקב״ה made him age suddenly so that his death would look natural and דוד could reign on time. The גמרא proves that one person can be pushed aside for another. Then comes a story of רב נחמן and רבי יצחק at a meal. It includes the rule not to talk while eating, the teaching that יעקב אבינו did not die, and a statement about רחב. At parting, רבי יצחק begins a משל about a perfect tree to explain how to bless רב נחמן, and the ברכה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Idol worship counts as two evils
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the earlier question: the 'two evils' in the פסוק are really one sin, עבודה זרה, which weighs as much as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is one sin that is equal to two. What is it? Idol worship. As it says: 'For My people have done two evils: they left Me, the source of living water, to dig for themselves broken cisterns.' And it says about them: 'Cross over to the islands of כתים and see, send to קדר and look carefully. Has any nation exchanged its gods, even though they are not real gods? But My people exchanged its glory for something worthless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to רב נחמן's earlier question about the 'two evils' in ירמיהו. It says the two evils are really one sin, עבודה זרה, which is as bad as two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק names two parts of one act: leaving ה׳, and turning to 'broken cisterns' that hold nothing. The second פסוק sharpens the point. Other nations never trade away even their false gods, yet the Jewish people traded away the true God for something useless.

keyTerms.meaning: Broken cisterns, pits that cannot hold water
For something that does not help, something worthless

phrases.english: [There is one sin] equivalent to two,
and what is it? Idol worship,
as it is written: "For My people have committed two evils;
they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters,
to hew for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns,"
and it is written about them:
"For pass over the isles of Kittim and see,
and send to Kedar and observe carefully, etc.

phrases.aramaic: הַהֵימִיר גּוֹי אֱלֹהִים וְהֵמָּה לֹא אֱלֹהִים
phrases.english: Has a nation exchanged its gods, although they are no gods?
But My people has exchanged its glory for that which does not profit."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקוּלָה כִּשְׁתַּיִם, וּמַאי נִיהוּ — עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer to רב נחמן's question from the previous section about the 'two evils.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'two evils' are one sin, עבודה זרה, which is as bad as two.

steps.title: The nations kept their gods even when they knew better
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the comparison in the פסוק. The people of כתים worship fire and the people of קדר worship water, yet neither switched gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the people of כתים worship fire, and the people of קדר worship water. Even though they know that water puts out fire, they did not switch their gods. 'But My people exchanged its glory for something worthless.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא fills in the details of the פסוק about כתים and קדר. It shows how stubbornly loyal those nations are to their false gods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire worshippers could see that water 'beats' fire, so they had a reason to switch, yet they never did. The Jewish people, by contrast, left the one true God for nothing. This makes the sin of עבודה זרה even worse.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the people of the islands of כתים

steps.confusionAlert: Here כותיים does NOT mean the Samaritans, as it usually does in גמרא. It refers to the people of כתים from the פסוק.

phrases.english: It was taught: The Kittites worship fire,
and the people of Kedar worship water,
and even though they know
that water extinguishes fire,
they have not exchanged their gods:
"But My people has exchanged its glory for that which does not profit."

steps.whatToRemember: עבודה זרה by the Jewish people is 'two evils.' Even idol-worshipping nations stay loyal to their gods, yet Israel abandoned the true God.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the comparison to כתים and קדר in the פסוק quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nations that worship fire and water never switched gods, even though water defeats fire. Israel's switch is therefore far worse.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks about שמואל being old
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן opens a new topic and asks רבי יצחק what the פסוק means when it says שמואל was old.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'And it was when שמואל was old'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts a new question about a פסוק concerning שמואל. This line sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this is only a request to explain the פסוק. The real difficulty, that שמואל was not actually old, is spelled out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And it came to pass when Samuel was old"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same series of questions רב נחמן asked רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the פסוק call שמואל 'old'?

steps.title: שמואל died at only fifty-two
steps.stepSummary: The difficulty: שמואל died at fifty-two, so how could the פסוק call him old?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really get that old? He was only fifty-two! As the Master said: someone who dies at fifty-two, that is the death of שמואל from רמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the פסוק by bringing a teaching that shows שמואל died at fifty-two, which is not old age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching treats fifty-two as 'the age שמואל died.' If he never lived past fifty-two, calling him 'old' seems wrong. That is the problem רבי יצחק must now answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an accepted teaching)

phrases.english: And did Samuel really grow so old?
But he was only fifty-two years old,
as the Master said:
One who dies at fifty-two years,
this is the death of Samuel of Rama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out why the פסוק in step 3 is difficult.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'when שמואל was old' (שמואל א 8:1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An accepted teaching shows שמואל died at fifty-two, which is too young to be called old.

steps.title: Old age jumped on שמואל early
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן: old age came on שמואל suddenly and early, connected to ה׳ regretting that He made שאול king.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: Old age jumped onto him, as it says, 'I regret that I made שאול king.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question. שמואל really was young in years, but old age 'jumped' on him early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps both facts. שמואל died at fifty-two, but he aged before his time. The פסוק about ה׳ regretting שאול's kingship points to the event that caused this, and the next step explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Old age jumped on him (he aged suddenly and early)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rabbi Yochanan said as follows:
Old age sprang upon him,
as it is written: "I regret that I made Saul king."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זִקְנָה קָפְצָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'old' describes his early aging, not his number of years.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Old' means שמואל lived many years, which clashes with his death at fifty-two.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was young in years, but old age came on him early because of what happened with שאול.

steps.title: שמואל asks that his work not be undone in his lifetime
steps.stepSummary: שמואל pleads with ה׳. Since ה׳ compared him to משה and אהרן, whose work was never undone while they lived, his own work should not be undone while he lives either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before ה׳: Master of the World! You counted me as equal to משה and אהרן, as it says, 'משה and אהרן among His כהנים, and שמואל among those who call His Name.' Just as the work of משה and אהרן was not undone while they lived, so too let my work not be undone while I live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins telling what happened between שמואל and ה׳‎. שמואל asks that his work, making שאול king, not be cancelled while he is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל builds his request on a פסוק in תהלים that lists him together with משה and אהרן. If they are equal, the same treatment should apply to him: his work should stay standing during his lifetime. Steps 7 and 8 explain how this request led to his early aging.

keyTerms.meaning: You weighed me, You counted me as equal
The work of my hands, my accomplishments

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Master of the Universe!
You have considered me the equivalent of Moses and Aaron,
as it is written: "Moses and Aaron among His priests,
and Samuel among those who call upon His Name."
Just as Moses and Aaron,
their handiwork was not annulled in their lifetimes,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֲנִי לֹא יִתְבַּטֵּל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי בְּחַיַּי.
phrases.english: so too, let my handiwork not be annulled in my lifetime.
phrases.notes: He means שאול, whom he anointed as king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יוחנן's answer in step 5 by telling the story behind שמואל's early aging.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל argues that, since he is equal to משה and אהרן, his work (שאול's kingship) should not be undone in his lifetime.

steps.title: ה׳'s dilemma: three options that all seem blocked
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה weighs three options: let שאול die, let שמואל die young, or let neither die. Each one runs into a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה said: What should I do? If שאול dies, שמואל won't allow it. If שמואל dies young, people will gossip about him. If neither dies, there is a problem, because the time for דוד's kingdom has already come, and one kingdom may not cut into the next one's time even by a hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes הקב״ה thinking through a problem with no easy way out. It is setting up the solution that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's prayer protects שאול, so שאול cannot die yet. שמואל dying young would make people suspect he sinned. Keeping both alive would push into דוד's time, and kingdoms cannot overlap at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They will gossip about him, wondering what sin he did
One kingdom does not cut into the time of another
Even the width of a hair

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
What shall I do?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימוּת שָׁאוּל — לָא קָא שָׁבֵיק שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Shall Saul die? Samuel will not allow it,
phrases.notes: שמואל had prayed that שאול should not die while he himself was alive.

phrases.english: Shall Samuel die while still young?
People will murmur about him.

phrases.aramaic: לָא לֵימוּת שָׁאוּל וְלָא לֵימוּת שְׁמוּאֵל —
phrases.english: Shall neither Saul nor Samuel die?
The time of David's kingdom has already arrived,
and one kingdom does not touch another
even by a hairbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: הֵיכִי אֶעֱבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to שמואל's plea in step 6 that his work not be undone in his lifetime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three simple options are blocked: שאול cannot die, שמואל cannot die young, and both cannot live on into דוד's time.

steps.title: The solution: sudden old age for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה decides to make שמואל age suddenly, so that his death will look natural.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה said: I will make old age jump onto him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the way out of the dilemma from step 7. שמואל will look old, so when he dies no one will gossip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Early aging fixes the second problem: people will think שמואל died of old age, not because of a sin. This also explains the question from step 4, how a fifty-two-year-old could be called old.

keyTerms.meaning: I will make it jump on suddenly

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I will spring old age upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the three-way dilemma of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A creative fourth option that avoids all three problems
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed every option was blocked.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל ages suddenly and dies looking old, so no one gossips, and דוד's kingdom comes on time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to step 4 and fully explains why the פסוק calls שמואל old at only fifty-two.

steps.title: A פסוק hints that שמואל's prayer kept שאול alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads a פסוק that puts שאול in both גבעה and רמה as a hint that the prayer of שמואל of רמה kept שאול in power.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'And שאול was sitting in גבעה under the tamarisk tree in רמה.' What does גבעה have to do with רמה? They are different places. It is teaching you: who caused שאול to stay ruling in גבעה for two and a half years? The prayer of שמואל from רמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the story that שמואל's prayer kept שאול alive. It points out something odd in the פסוק and explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גבעה and רמה are two separate places, so a person cannot sit 'in גבעה, in רמה.' The גמרא answers that 'רמה' points to שמואל, who came from רמה. His prayer is what let שאול remain in גבעה for those extra years.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what is written; this explains the פסוק
What does this have to do with that?
Rather, it comes to teach you
The one from Rama, meaning שמואל

phrases.english: This is what is written:
"And Saul dwelled in Gibeah
under the tamarisk tree in Rama."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן גִּבְעָה אֵצֶל רָמָה?
phrases.english: What does Gibeah have to do with Rama?
Rather, it is to tell you:
Who caused Saul
to dwell in Gibeah for two and a half years?
The prayer of Samuel of Rama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the story from a פסוק, showing שמואל's prayer protected שאול.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל's prayer kept שאול alive and ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 22:6, where גבעה and רמה appear together

steps.title: Can one person really be pushed aside for another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it is fair or possible that שמואל's life is cut short just because דוד's time has come.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is one person really pushed aside because of another person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. It finds it hard to accept that שמואל would die early only to make room for דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we think a person's lifespan depends on his own deeds. Here שמואל seems to lose years because of someone else's schedule, and the גמרא questions that.

keyTerms.meaning: And is someone really pushed aside?
One man because of another man

phrases.english: And is one man set aside before another man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the idea behind the solution in steps 7-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל's life was shortened because דוד's kingdom had arrived
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person's life should depend on his own deeds, not on making room for someone else.

steps.title: Yes, a פסוק in הושע shows it happens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and proves from a פסוק that הקב״ה sometimes ends a person's life by His word, not because of the person's deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק mean, 'Therefore I cut down through the prophets, I killed them with the words of My mouth'? It does not say 'because of their deeds,' but 'with the words of My mouth.' So we see that one person can be pushed aside because of another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10 with a clear yes, and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the exact wording: the פסוק says the deaths came 'by the words of My mouth,' not 'by their deeds.' That shows a death can come from הקב״ה's decree and plan, not only as punishment. So שמואל's early death makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: By the words of My mouth

steps.whatToRemember: A person's life can sometimes end because of הקב״ה's larger plan, not because of his own sins. That is how שמואל could die early to make room for דוד.

phrases.english: Yes,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Therefore I have hewn by the prophets,
I have slain them by the words of My mouth"?
"By their deeds" is not stated,
but rather "by the words of My mouth."
Apparently, one man is set aside before another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 directly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and proves it from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person's death should only come because of his own deeds.
steps.terutzMaskana: A death can come by הקב״ה's word alone, so one person can be pushed aside for another.

steps.title: At a meal, רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק to say some Torah
steps.stepSummary: A new short story begins: רב נחמן and רבי יצחק are eating together, and רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק to share a Torah thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רבי יצחק were sitting at a meal. רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: Let the master say something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new story between the same two חכמים from step 3. This step sets up רבי יצחק's surprising answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן keeps asking רבי יצחק to teach him, as he did in step 3. Here he asks during a meal, which sets up the lesson about whether one may talk while eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master say something, meaning a Torah thought

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוּדְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman and Rabbi Yitzḥak were sitting at a meal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Rabbi Yitzḥak:
Let the master say a matter.
phrases.notes: He is asking for a Torah idea.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוּדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story between the same two חכמים as in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah thought from רבי יצחק during the meal

steps.title: No talking while eating, because of the danger of choking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן that one should not talk during a meal, because food might go down the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: We do not talk during a meal, because the windpipe might open before the food pipe, and the person could come into danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers רב נחמן's request by explaining why he will not talk now. Talking while eating can make a person choke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food should go down the food pipe. When a person talks, the windpipe opens, and food can slip in there and cause choking. So רבי יצחק turns down the request, and his answer is itself a teaching.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule about safety at meals, taught through a story.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: So said Rabbi Yoḥanan:
One may not speak during a meal,
lest the windpipe come before the food pipe,
phrases.notes: Talking opens the windpipe, so food might go down the wrong way.

phrases.english: and he will come into danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מְסִיחִין בִּסְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יצחק's reply to רב נחמן's request in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He declines to talk, quoting רבי יוחנן that talking during a meal risks choking.

steps.title: After the meal: יעקב our father did not die
steps.stepSummary: Once the meal is over, רבי יצחק shares the Torah thought he held back during it: רבי יוחנן taught that יעקב אבינו did not die.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they had eaten, he said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: Our father יעקב did not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The meal is finished, so now רבי יצחק is free to talk, and he shares a surprising teaching from רבי יוחנן: יעקב אבינו did not die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13 he refused to talk during the meal, and this step shows he kept his word by waiting until afterward. The claim is bold because the תורה describes יעקב's death and burial. That sets up the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: After they had eaten, he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יצחק is speaking. He waited until the meal was over, just as he said in Step 13.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
Our father Yaakov did not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דִּסְעוּד אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fulfills the request from Step 12. The Torah thought held back during the meal in Step 13 is now shared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן teaches that יעקב אבינו did not die.

steps.title: But יעקב was eulogized, embalmed and buried
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges the teaching: if יעקב did not die, why was he eulogized, embalmed and buried?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed, and the buriers buried?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back. Everyone saw that יעקב was mourned, embalmed and buried, so how can anyone say he did not die?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge uses facts from the תורה's own story of יעקב's funeral. If he were alive, all of those funeral acts would have been pointless. The question forces רבי יצחק to explain what 'did not die' means.

phrases.english: He said to him: Was it for nothing
that the eulogizers eulogized,
and the embalmers embalmed,
phrases.notes: The embalming of יעקב is described in בראשית 50:2-3.

phrases.english: and the buriers buried?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the claim made in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that יעקב אבינו did not die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה records that יעקב was eulogized, embalmed and buried, and those acts only make sense if he died.

steps.title: A verse links יעקב to his living children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers that he is expounding a פסוק that places יעקב alongside his descendants. Since his descendants are alive, he is alive too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I am explaining a verse, as it says, 'And you, do not fear, My servant יעקב, says ה׳, and do not be dismayed, Israel, for I will save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity.' The verse compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק says this is not about what people saw at the funeral. It comes from a פסוק that puts יעקב and his children together, and since his children are alive, יעקב is described as alive too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק does not deny the funeral. He answers that his source is a פסוק and not what people observed. The tool he uses is a היקש, which means two things mentioned together are treated alike. יעקב is saved together with his living descendants, so he shares their status of being 'alive'.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק never says the funeral did not happen. He is giving the source of the teaching, not arguing about what people saw.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am explaining a verse,
as it is said: "And you, do not fear,
My servant Yaakov, says ה׳,
and do not be dismayed, Israel,
for I will save you from afar,
and your seed from the land of their captivity."
It compares him to his seed:
just as his seed is alive,
so too he is alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by revealing the scriptural source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The claim seemed to contradict the plain facts of יעקב's funeral.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim comes from a פסוק that pairs יעקב with his living descendants, so he too is called alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about the eternal life of יעקב אבינו.

steps.title: The power of saying רחב's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק shares a second teaching: anyone who says the name רחב twice immediately has a seminal emission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Anyone who says 'רחב, רחב' immediately has a seminal emission.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק makes a new and striking statement about how strongly the name רחב affects a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic and is not tied to יעקב. The statement is extreme and universal ('anyone who says'), which leaves it open to the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: the woman from יְרִיחוֹ in the book of יְהוֹשֻׁעַ

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who says "Rachav, Rachav"
phrases.notes: רחב is the woman in יריחו who hid the spies, in יהושע 2.

phrases.english: immediately has a seminal emission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching shared during the same visit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying the name רחב twice brings on an immediate emission.

steps.title: רב נחמן says it does not affect him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges the statement from his own experience: he says the name and nothing happens to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I say it and it does not affect me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tests the claim on himself. He says he says the name רחב and it does nothing to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement said 'anyone', so a single person it does not happen to is enough to challenge it. רב נחמן is himself that person.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
I say it, and it does not affect me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sweeping statement of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that anyone who says 'רחב, רחב' is affected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Personal experience: רב נחמן says it and is not affected, so the word 'anyone' cannot be right.

steps.title: It applies only to someone who knew her
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק narrows his statement: he meant only a man who knew רחב and recognized her in person.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When I said it, I meant someone who knew her and recognized her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that his statement was never about everyone. It was only about men who actually knew רחב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer limits who the statement applies to. רב נחמן never met רחב, so he is not included, and the challenge falls away while the teaching stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: when I said it (what I meant was)
about one who knew her and recognized her

phrases.english: He said to him: When I said it,
I meant one who knew her and recognized her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by limiting the scope of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (narrowing who the statement applies to)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement seemed to apply to every person who says the name.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to someone who personally knew רחב.

steps.title: At parting, רב נחמן asks for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: As the two part, רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק to bless him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they were taking leave of each other, he said to him: Let the master bless me!
steps.whatsHappening: The visit is ending, and רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק for a ברכה. This sets up the parable that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request, not a challenge. It opens the closing scene of the story, and רבי יצחק will answer with a משל rather than a plain ברכה.

phrases.english: When they were taking leave of each other,
he said to him: Let the master bless me!
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is the one asking, and he calls רבי יצחק 'master' out of respect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the end of the visit that began in Step 12.

steps.title: The parable of the tired traveler and the tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers with a משל: a hungry, tired and thirsty traveler in the desert finds a perfect tree and enjoys its fruit, water and shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I will tell you a parable. What is this like? A man was walking in the desert, hungry, tired and thirsty. He found a tree with sweet fruit and pleasant shade, and a stream of water flowing under it. He ate its fruit, drank its water and sat in its shade.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of giving a ברכה right away, רבי יצחק starts a story. The story sets up how he will bless רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each need of the traveler (hunger, tiredness, thirst) is matched by something the tree gives (fruit, shade, water). The tree stands for רב נחמן, the one asking for a ברכה, who already has everything good.

keyTerms.meaning: I will tell you a parable

phrases.english: He said to him: I will tell you a parable.
To what is this comparable?
To a person who was walking in the desert,
and he was hungry, tired and thirsty.
And he found a tree whose fruits were sweet,
and its shade was pleasant,
and a stream of water flowed beneath it.
He ate from its fruits,
drank from its water,
and sat in its shade.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the request for a ברכה in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer opens with a משל of a traveler and a perfect tree.

steps.title: What blessing can you give a tree that has everything?
steps.stepSummary: Leaving the tree, the traveler wonders how to bless it, since it already has sweet fruit, nice shade and water. He decides to bless the saplings planted from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he wanted to leave, he said: Tree, tree, with what shall I bless you? If I say your fruits should be sweet, they are already sweet. If I say your shade should be pleasant, it is already pleasant. If I say a stream should flow beneath you, one already flows beneath you. Rather, may it be God's will that all the saplings planted from you...
steps.whatsHappening: The traveler wants to thank the tree with a ברכה, but every blessing he thinks of is something the tree already has. So he turns to blessing its saplings, and the sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traveler goes through each gift (fruit, shade, water) and shows that blessing it adds nothing. That leaves only one meaningful ברכה: for the tree's offspring. This hints at how רבי יצחק will bless רב נחמן, who already has everything.

keyTerms.meaning: with what shall I bless you?

steps.whatToRemember: The משל teaches that when someone already has every blessing, the best ברכה is that his offspring be like him.

phrases.english: And when he wanted to leave, he said:
Tree, tree, with what shall I bless you?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אוֹמַר לְךָ שֶׁיְּהוּ פֵּירוֹתֶיךָ מְתוּקִין —
phrases.english: If I say to you that your fruits should be sweet,
your fruits are already sweet.
That your shade should be pleasant,
your shade is already pleasant.
That a stream of water should flow beneath you,
a stream of water already flows beneath you.
Rather: may it be [God's] will
that all the saplings which are planted from you

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משל from Step 21 and moves toward the actual ברכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the tree already has everything, the only meaningful ברכה is for its saplings. The ending continues past this point.
